relevance_reason: The paper reports a new patient with Mitchell-Riley syndrome who carried a novel homozygous RFX6 mutation, with detailed clinical features.

findings.statement: Concepcion et al. (2014) described a male infant born at 34 weeks' gestation to nonconsanguineous Vietnamese parents. Prenatally he had intrauterine growth restriction and duodenal atresia. He was small for gestational age (birth weight 1375 g) and had severe hyperglycemia (446 mg/dL) within 24 hours of birth, which needed an insulin infusion. He had low C-peptide, low amylase and lipase, and low stool pancreatic elastase. Laparotomy on day 5 confirmed duodenal atresia, intestinal malrotation, and jejunal perforation, and ultrasound suggested an annular pancreas.
quotes: Our patient was a male infant born at 34 weeks gestation to non-consanguineous Vietnamese parents, with no known family history of diabetes mellitus, familial intestinal disorders, or early death (UC proband 0250). Prenatally, he was known to have intrauterine growth restriction and duodenal atresia.
He underwent urgent exploratory laparotomy, which confirmed duodenal atresia, intestinal malrotation, and jejunal perforation.

Additional laboratory tests included a low C-peptide level (0.25 ng/mL at 10 days of life, with blood glucose of 246 mg/dL; normal 0.4–2.2 ng/mL), low amylase (8 units/L; normal 36–128 units/L), low lipase (13 units/L; normal 22–51 units/L)

findings.statement: Concepcion et al. (2014) reported that the patient's course included cholestatic jaundice, recurrent infections, feeding intolerance, and severe chronic diarrhea that needed intermittent parenteral nutrition and did not improve with pancreatic enzymes. Laparotomy at 3 months showed gallbladder agenesis. A hepatobiliary scan did not visualize the gallbladder or common bile duct, and liver biopsy showed bile ductular proliferation. He developed liver failure and died of sepsis at 5 months of age while awaiting liver transplantation.
quotes: He had a prolonged neonatal course, complicated by cholestatic jaundice, recurrent infections, and feeding intolerance.
At three months old, a repeat exploratory laparotomy for abdominal distension revealed gallbladder agenesis.
He was transferred to University of California Los Angeles for liver transplant evaluation due to liver failure, but unfortunately died at five months of age secondary to sepsis prior to transplant.

findings.statement: In a Vietnamese boy with Mitchell-Riley syndrome, Concepcion et al. (2014) used whole-exome sequencing and found a novel homozygous missense mutation in RFX6, c.779A>C (p.Lys260Thr; K260T). Sanger sequencing confirmed the mutation, and both parents were heterozygous carriers. The variant was absent from dbSNP and 1000 Genomes. It affects a highly conserved lysine and was predicted to be damaging. It also changes the consensus 5-prime splice donor site of intron 7, which was predicted to disrupt splicing. Runs of homozygosity suggested that the parents might be distantly related.
quotes: whole exome sequencing revealed a novel homozygous RFX6 mutation c.779A>C; p.Lys260Thr (K260T). This missense mutation also changes the consensus 5' splice donor site before intron 7 and is thus predicted to cause disruption in splicing. Both parents, who were not known to be related, were heterozygous carriers.
Two analysis tools (www.fruitfly.org/seq_tools/splice.html and www.cbs.dtu.dk/services/NetGene2/) predicted that the mutant sequence is no longer likely to be used as a 5’ donor splice site.
The fact that this RFX6 variant is not present in publically available repositories (1000 genomes, dbSNP) suggests that it is rare and that the parents of the proband may be distantly related.

findings.statement: In a review of 8 patients with RFX6 mutations, Concepcion et al. (2014) noted that the 2 longest survivors were a compound heterozygote with 2 splice site mutations and a patient with a homozygous missense mutation that reduced but did not abolish DNA binding. These 2 patients also had the highest birth weights. In contrast, the authors' patient had disease as severe as patients with homozygous splice site, frameshift, or DNA-binding-abolishing mutations. They noted that chronic diarrhea had been reported in most patients with RFX6 mutations.
quotes: The longest surviving case (Proband 3, alive at 9 years), was the only compound heterozygote, with two different splice site mutations, while the next oldest (Proband 2, alive at 6 years) had a homozygous missense mutation that was shown to reduce but not abrogate DNA binding.
This genotype-phenotype correlation is also reflected in the birth weights of these two cases being the highest of any reported.
Although chronic diarrhea has been reported in the majority of cases with RFX6 mutations (Table 1), it has not been emphasized as a consistent feature of the syndrome.

relevance_reason: Case report of an infant with Mitchell-Riley syndrome carrying a novel homozygous RFX6 missense mutation.

findings.statement: Zegre Amorim et al. (2015) reported a girl born to first-cousin Gipsy parents. Prenatal ultrasound showed intrauterine growth restriction and a 'double bubble'. She was born at 35 weeks with weight, length, and head circumference below the 3rd centile. She developed hyperglycemia on day 2 and needed continuous insulin. On day 3, insulin and C-peptide levels were very low, and GAD, islet cell, and IA-2 autoantibodies were negative. Laparotomy on day 4 confirmed type II duodenal atresia with annular pancreas, malrotation, and gallbladder agenesis.
quotes: We report a girl, the second child of first-cousin Gipsy parents.
On day 2 hyperglycemia (415 mg/dL) occurred, requiring continuous insulin infusion along with parenteral nutrition with glucose rates around 5-6 mg/Kg/min.
On day 4 laparotomy confirmed duodenal atresia (type II) that was associated with annular pancreas, malrotation, and gallbladder agenesis.

findings.statement: Zegre Amorim et al. (2015) reported that the patient developed cholestasis from day 6, with conjugated bilirubin of 3.07 mg/dL and GGT of 458 IU/L; it resolved without treatment by 2 months of age. Ultrasound showed biliary duct dilation, and the head of the pancreas was disproportionately large with an unidentifiable tail. At surgery, perijejunal submucosal tissue that looked like ectopic pancreatic tissue was seen; the authors described this as a novel feature, but it was not biopsied. The patient had chronic diarrhea and malabsorption that did not respond to exocrine pancreatic supplementation. At 7 months she had failure to thrive and still depended on insulin and partial parenteral nutrition.
quotes: From D6 cholestasis appeared and progressively worsened reaching levels of conjugated bilirubin of 3.07 mg/dL, gamma-glutamyl transpeptidase of 458 IU/L
Perijejunal tissue in the submucosa was found with macroscopic appearance of ectopic pancreatic tissue
Currently she is seven months old and still has malabsorption with failure to thrive (weight 4865 g).

findings.statement: In a girl with Mitchell-Riley syndrome born to consanguineous Gipsy parents, Zegre Amorim et al. (2015) used Sanger sequencing to identify a homozygous missense mutation in exon 4 of the RFX6 gene (c.541C>T, p.R181W). Both parents were heterozygous for the mutation. The arginine at codon 181 lies in the DNA-binding domain and is highly conserved across species. The authors noted that a different mutation at the same residue (p.R181Q) had been reported previously.
quotes: A homozygous missense mutation was identified on exon 4, c.541C>T, p.R181W in the proband. Both parents are heterozygous.
The arginine residue at codon 181, located in the DNA binding domain, is highly conserved across species and this change affects protein function.
A different mutation at the same residue has already been reported in patients with Mitchell-Riley syndrome (p.R181Q).

findings.statement: Zegre Amorim et al. (2015) reported a proband born to first-cousin parents, both of whom were heterozygous for the RFX6 mutation. The mother had previously had 3 first-trimester spontaneous abortions and a child with isolated congenital anorectal malformation.
quotes: Before the proband, the 28-year-old mother had 3 spontaneous abortions in the first trimester and a child with isolated congenital anorectal malformation.

relevance_reason: The paper identifies RFX6 mutations in infants with autosomal recessive neonatal diabetes, intestinal atresia and gallbladder hypoplasia, and proposes the name Mitchell-Riley syndrome. It also describes the Rfx6 knockout mouse model.

findings.statement: Smith et al. (2010) described human patients with neonatal diabetes and small bowel obstruction due to bowel atresia. Pancreas size was somewhat reduced, but exocrine pancreatic enzymes were not deficient. Autopsy in 2 cases showed normal-appearing exocrine pancreas with clusters of chromogranin A-positive cells but no cells staining for insulin, glucagon, or somatostatin. The syndrome also included a hypoplastic gallbladder and intractable diarrhea that did not respond to pancreatic enzyme replacement.
quotes: The phenotype of the Rfx6 eGFPcre/eGFPcre mice is remarkably similar to human patients born with neonatal diabetes and small bowel obstruction due to bowel atresia.

Despite some reduction in pancreatic size, these cases were not deficient in enzymes of the exocrine pancreas, and autopsies of two cases (proband #1 and case 3 in Ref) revealed normal-appearing exocrine pancreata with clusters of ChromograninA-positive cells but total absence of cells staining for insulin, glucagon, or somatostatin.
In addition, the syndrome involves hypoplastic gall bladder, and intractable diarrhea unresponsive to pancreatic enzyme replacement.

phenotypes.text: absence of islet insulin, glucagon and somatostatin cells
phenotypes.hpo_label: Abnormality of the pancreatic islet cells

findings.statement: Smith et al. (2010) noted that OMIM listed their patients under Martinez-Frias syndrome. They considered the cases distinct, because the original Martinez-Frias patients had esophageal atresia and hypospadias without diabetes, and no RFX6 mutation was found in the parents of 1 Martinez-Frias case. They proposed the name Mitchell-Riley syndrome, after the 2 clinicians who first described the condition.
quotes: However, since the original MFS patients also had oesophageal atresia and hypospadias, and did not have diabetes, and we did not find any RFX6 mutation in the parents of one case of MFS, our cases are distinct from MFS.
We propose to name their condition, now of defined molecular aetiology, the Mitchell-Riley syndrome after the two clinicians who first described it.

findings.statement: Smith et al. (2010) performed high-resolution homozygosity mapping in 2 probands whose parents were first and second cousins, respectively. They found 10 homozygosity-by-descent (HBD) segments larger than 500 kb in proband 1 and 25 in proband 2. Only 3 HBD regions, totaling 24 Mb, were shared (2p15-16, 6q21-22, and 6q23). Of the 194 RefSeq genes in these regions, only RFX6, in the largest segment at 6q21-22, had pancreas-enriched expression.
quotes: The disease locus was mapped using overlapping homozygosity in probands #1and #2 (see Supplementary material for pedigree information and references to previous clinical case reports) respectively the offspring of first and second cousins.
Only three HBD regions were common in the two probands, totaling 24 Mb (Table 1).
Of these genes, only RFX6, which falls in the largest segment at 6q21-22, had pancreas–enriched expression in the TiGER database (Supplementary Table 6)

findings.statement: In proband 2, the child of consanguineous parents, Smith et al. (2010) used array capture and deep sequencing of the exons within the 3 shared HBD regions. Of 30 novel variants, the only nonsynonymous change was a homozygous ser217-to-pro (S217P) substitution in RFX6, and direct sequencing confirmed it. The patient was alive at age 4.5 years. The variant lies between the DNA-binding and dimerization domains. In EMSA it only modestly reduced DNA binding, and it did not affect dimer formation.
quotes: The only non-synonymous variant was 217 Ser>Pro in RFX6, identifying this gene as the most likely candidate.
Proband #2, still alive at age 4.5 years, had the homozygous missense mutation 217 Ser>Pro, confirming the unbiased exon sequencing described above.
while 217S>P (proband #2), which lies between the DNA-binding domain and dimerization domain of Rfx6, only modestly reduced DNA binding (Fig. 5d) and did not affect dimer formation (data not shown).

findings.statement: Smith et al. (2010) found a homozygous splice donor mutation in intron 2 of RFX6 (IVS2+2T-C) in proband 1, the child of first cousins, who died in the first few months of life. RT-PCR of RNA from the patient's autopsy pancreas detected no properly spliced RFX6 transcript. No RNA was detected from exons 1 and 2, which the authors attributed probably to nonsense-mediated decay.
quotes: Probands #1, 4 and 5 all died in the first few months of life and were homozygous for, respectively, a loss of the donor splicing site in intron 2 (IVS2+2 t>c), an out-of-frame deletion in exon 7, and the missense mutation 181 R>Q
we amplified RFX6 mRNA by RT-PCR of high-quality RNA from autopsy pancreas and failed to detect the properly spliced transcript, which was easily amplified from normal foetal pancreas
We also failed to detect any RNA from exons 1+2, upstream of the splicing mutation, probably due to nonsense-mediated decay(Supplementary Fig. S16).

findings.statement: Smith et al. (2010) found a homozygous out-of-frame deletion in exon 7 of RFX6 in proband 4, who died in the first few months of life. The mutation was inherited from carrier parents.
quotes: Probands #1, 4 and 5 all died in the first few months of life and were homozygous for, respectively, a loss of the donor splicing site in intron 2 (IVS2+2 t>c), an out-of-frame deletion in exon 7, and the missense mutation 181 R>Q
All mutations were inherited from carrier parents.

findings.statement: Smith et al. (2010) found a homozygous arg181-to-gln (R181Q) missense mutation in RFX6 in proband 5, who died in the first few months of life. The mutation affects a highly conserved arginine in the DNA-binding domain. In EMSA, the mutation completely abolished DNA binding by RFX6.
quotes: the missense mutation 181 R>Q involving a highly conserved arginine in the DNA-binding domain (Supplementary Fig. S15)
We found that 181R>Q (proband #5), which alters a conserved amino acid in the DNA binding domain, completely abrogated DNA binding

findings.statement: Smith et al. (2010) found that proband 3 was compound heterozygous for 2 RFX6 splice mutations: loss of the donor site in intron 6 (IVS6+2T-G) and disruption of the acceptor site in intron 1 (IVS1-12A-G). The patient was alive at age 9 years and intermittently off insulin. The mutations were inherited from carrier parents.
quotes: Proband #3, still alive at the age of 9 and intermittently off insulin, was a compound heterozygote for donor-site loss in intron 6 (IVS6+2 t>g) and disruption of the acceptor site in intron 1 (IVS1-12 a>g).
All mutations were inherited from carrier parents.

findings.statement: Smith et al. (2010) sequenced the 19 exons and splice junctions of RFX6 directly and found missense, splicing, or frameshift mutations in 5 of 6 available probands with the syndrome. All mutations were inherited from carrier parents.
quotes: Missense, splicing or frameshift mutations in RFX6 were found in five of the six available probands (Fig. 5e) with an interesting genotype-phenotype correlation.
All mutations were inherited from carrier parents.

findings.statement: Smith et al. (2010) reported a genotype-phenotype correlation. The 3 probands homozygous for a splice donor loss, a frameshift deletion, or the R181Q mutation (which abolished DNA binding) all died in the first few months of life. The 2 longer survivors were the patient homozygous for S217P, which only modestly reduced DNA binding (alive at 4.5 years), and the compound heterozygote for 2 splice-site mutations (alive at 9 years and intermittently off insulin).
quotes: Probands #1, 4 and 5 all died in the first few months of life and were homozygous for, respectively, a loss of the donor splicing site in intron 2 (IVS2+2 t>c), an out-of-frame deletion in exon 7, and the missense mutation 181 R>Q
Proband #3, still alive at the age of 9 and intermittently off insulin, was a compound heterozygote

findings.statement: Smith et al. (2010) found no RFX6 mutation in proband 6. Proband DNA was unavailable; neither parent carried a point mutation in RFX6 or NEUROG3, and long-range PCR showed no RFX6 deletion. The authors could not rule out a de novo mutation but considered the case most likely a phenocopy. They also found no RFX6 mutation in a case of Martinez-Frias syndrome.
quotes: In the absence of DNA from the proband, we sequenced both parents and found no point mutation of RFX6 or NEUROG3; and long-range PCR did not reveal any deletions of RFX6 (Supplementary Fig. S17).
In the absence of proband DNA we cannot rule out a de novo mutation, but this case is most likely a phenocopy. We also failed to find RFX6 mutations in a case of the Martinez-Frias syndrome.

findings.statement: Smith et al. (2010) generated Rfx6-null mice by replacing the first 5 exons, which include the DNA-binding domain, with an eGFP-cre cassette. Homozygous mice were born at the expected Mendelian ratio but fed poorly, had gross bowel distension from small bowel obstruction, and died within 2 days of birth; some had a reduced pancreas size. At embryonic day 17.5, mutant pancreata contained many chromogranin A-positive endocrine cells, but none expressed insulin, glucagon, somatostatin, or ghrelin. Pancreatic polypeptide-expressing cells were increased.
quotes: From heterozygous crosses, homozygous Rfx6eGFPcre/eGFPcre mice were born at the expected Mendelian ratio, but failed to feed normally, exhibited gross bowel distension due to small bowel obstruction (Fig. 3e-f) and died within 2 days post partum.

Immunofluorescence staining with the endocrine markers Chromogranin A or Synaptophysin at e17.5 demonstrated that the Rfx6 eGFPcre/eGFPcre pancreata still contained a large number of endocrine cells, but confirmed that none of these cells expressed insulin, glucagon, somatostatin or ghrelin (Fig. 4).

findings.statement: Smith et al. (2010) found that Rfx6 is expressed broadly in the definitive endoderm and later becomes restricted to the gut and pancreatic bud. It acts downstream of neurogenin-3 (Neurog3) and upstream of many islet transcription factors, and is required for the differentiation of 4 of the 5 islet cell types. Both RFX6 and NEUROG3 mutations cause diarrhea and diabetes. The authors attributed the small bowel atresia and biliary abnormalities seen only with RFX6 mutation to Rfx6 expression in the early gut endoderm, where neurogenin-3 is not expressed.
quotes: Like RFX6 mutations, mutation of NEUROG3 in humans also causes intractable diarrhoea and diabetes, but NEUROG3 mutation does not cause the small bowel atresia or biliary abnormalities seen with RFX6 mutation, which is not surprising since Neurogenin3 is not expressed in the early gut endoderm as is Rfx6.

we have identified a novel factor in endoderm and islet development, Rfx6, that is required for the differentiation of 4 of the 5 islet cell types and for the production of insulin in both humans and mice.

relevance_reason: A case report of a newborn with diabetes from pancreatic agenesis, gallbladder agenesis, duodenal malrotation and heart septal defects. This matches the Mitchell-Riley phenotype, but no RFX6 testing was done and IPF1 testing was negative.

findings.statement: Ashraf et al. (2005) reported an infant with neonatal diabetes due to pancreatic agenesis. The infant also had cardiac septal defects, gallbladder agenesis, and duodenal malrotation. The infant survived after treatment with insulin, exocrine pancreatic supplements, and surgical repair of the heart and intestinal anomalies.
quotes: We participated in the care of a patient with an unusual presentation of neonatal diabetes attributable to agenesis of the pancreas. Additional clinical features of the patient included cardiac septal defects, gall bladder agenesis and duodenal malrotation.
Appropriate institution of insulin, exocrine pancreatic supplements and surgical repair of the cardiac and intestinal anomalies resulted in the infant's survival.

findings.statement: In the infant with pancreatic agenesis, Ashraf et al. (2005) sequenced both coding exons of IPF1 and found no mutation. They suggested that the disturbance happened before the dorsal pancreatic bud appears, around embryonic day 25, which is before IPF1 is expressed.
quotes: Analysis of both exons of the Ipf-1 coding sequence from the presented patient's genomic DNA, however, did not identify a mutation.

These results suggest that a congenital or genetic perturbation occurred in this infant most likely before the appearance of dorsal pancreatic bud in the 3 mm long embryonic stage, around the embryonic day 25 in human development, before the onset of Ipf-1 expression.

relevance_reason: Reports two patients with Mitchell-Riley syndrome caused by compound heterozygous RFX6 nonsense mutations, with diabetes beginning in childhood rather than the neonatal period. It also reviews the previously reported cases.

findings.statement: Sansbury et al. (2015) reported 2 Turkish double first cousins with Mitchell-Riley syndrome whose diabetes was diagnosed at ages 3 and 6 years rather than in the neonatal period. The first was a girl born at 32 weeks' gestation with duodenal atresia, jejunal web and Meckel diverticulum. She had hyperglycemia at age 2 and presented with diabetic ketoacidosis at age 3, with very low insulin and C-peptide and negative autoantibodies. She also had an absent gallbladder and gastrointestinal bleeding due to gastric heterotopia in the small bowel. Her cousin, a boy born at 34 weeks with duodenal atresia and midgut malrotation, had asymptomatic fasting hyperglycemia at age 5 and was diagnosed with diabetes at age 6. He also had chronic iron deficiency anemia. Neither child had liver disease, and both were alive at age 9 years.
quotes: Case 1 (Figure 1, I5), current age 9 years, is a female born at 32 weeks' gestation, birth weight 1.65 kg (42nd centile), with duodenal atresia, jejunal web and Meckel's diverticulum.
She presented at the age of 3 years with diabetic ketoacidosis.

Case 2 (Figure 1, I12), her double first cousin, current age 9 years, is a male infant who was born at 34 weeks gestation, birth weight 1.70 kg (7th centile), with duodenal atresia and mid-gut malrotation. He was diagnosed with diabetes having presented with hyperglycemia (16.0 mmol/l) at the age of 6 years.

phenotypes.text: gastric heterotopia in small bowel with GI bleeding

findings.statement: In the 2 Turkish double first cousins with Mitchell-Riley syndrome and childhood-onset diabetes, Sansbury et al. (2015) used targeted next-generation sequencing of neonatal diabetes genes, with Sanger confirmation, to identify compound heterozygous RFX6 nonsense mutations. One was c.2176C>T (p.Arg726X) in exon 17, which the authors predicted to be subject to nonsense-mediated decay. The fathers were heterozygous for p.Arg726X, and the mutations were traced back to the grandmothers.
quotes: Genetic testing showed that both children are compound heterozygotes for the RFX6 nonsense mutations c.2176C>T (p.Arg726X) and c.2596C>T (p.Arg866X) in exons 17 and 18, respectively (Figure 2). The fathers were heterozygous for p.Arg726X and the mothers heterozygous for p.Arg866X.
The second mutation, c.2176C>T (R726X), is predicted to be subject to nonsense-mediated decay.

findings.statement: The second RFX6 mutation in the double first cousins described by Sansbury et al. (2015) was c.2596C>T (p.Arg866X) in exon 18, inherited from the mothers. Because it lies within 50 nucleotides of the last exon-exon boundary, the authors predicted that it escapes nonsense-mediated decay and yields a partially truncated protein that keeps the entire DNA-binding domain and may retain some function. These were the first RFX6 mutations reported in exons 9 to 19.
quotes: The exon 18 mutation, c.2596C>T (R866X) is predicted to escape nonsense-mediated decay because it lies within 50 nucleotides of the last exon–exon boundary of the gene.

A partially truncated version of the wild-type protein, which comprises 928 amino acids, is therefore predicted to be produced, possibly with some function given the full preservation of the DNA-binding domain.

findings.statement: Sansbury et al. (2015) noted that the 8 previously reported molecularly confirmed cases had splicing or frameshift mutations in exons 2 to 8, or missense mutations in or near the DNA-binding domain. They suggested a possible genotype-phenotype correlation in which escape from nonsense-mediated decay of the 3-prime p.Arg866X allele might preserve some RFX6 function, leading to later-onset diabetes and an otherwise milder phenotype.
quotes: Among the nine mutations identified in these eight cases (one a compound heterozygote, the remaining seven homozygous), six affect splicing and/or the reading frame in exons 2–8; the remaining three are mis-sense mutations clustering within or close to the DNA-binding domain (Figure 2).

It is possible that escape from NMD could lead to some retention of function of the RFX6 protein generated from that allele, with a resulting milder phenotype with respect to age of onset of diabetes and other clinical features.

findings.statement: In the family reported by Sansbury et al. (2015), several heterozygous relatives had adult-onset diabetes, but C-peptide levels in heterozygotes did not differ between those with and without diabetes. HbA1c also did not differ between non-diabetic heterozygotes and relatives without the familial mutation. The authors concluded that the data did not support heterozygosity for either RFX6 mutation as a risk factor for diabetes, although carriers of 5-prime mutations might still have an increased risk.
quotes: For heterozygotes in the family, there was no significant difference in C-peptide levels between those who had and had not developed diabetes.
Taking these data together, there is no support for the idea that being heterozygous for either RFX6 mutation is a risk factor for abnormal HbA1c or C-peptide levels, or diabetes.

findings.statement: Sansbury et al. (2015) reviewed 8 previously reported cases of Mitchell-Riley syndrome confirmed by biallelic RFX6 mutations. All had duodenal atresia, 7 of 8 had gallbladder agenesis, and all had liver involvement, with intrahepatic cholestasis in 7. Diabetes had begun within the first 2 weeks of life in all 8, and 5 had died within the first year of life.
quotes: Duodenal atresia is a present in all cases, with or without jejunal atresia/mid-gut malrotation. Gall-bladder agenesis is present in 7/8. All cases had evidence of liver involvement with intrahepatic cholestasis in 7/8 cases and ascites in a further case. Five of the eight children had died, all within the first year of life.

findings.statement: Sansbury et al. (2015) recommended considering genetic testing for RFX6 mutations in patients who present with intestinal atresias even when neonatal diabetes is absent, especially when there is evidence suggesting autosomal recessive inheritance.
quotes: Genetic testing for RFX6 mutations should be considered in patients presenting with intestinal atresias in the absence of neonatal diabetes, especially where sibling recurrence or parental consanguinity point to possible autosomal recessive inheritance.

relevance_reason: Reports sibs from a consanguineous family with duodenal atresia, extrahepatic biliary atresia, hypoplastic pancreas, and low birth weight. This overlaps with the Mitchell-Riley phenotype and points to autosomal recessive inheritance. No molecular data are given.

findings.statement: Martínez-Frías et al. (1992) described 2 sibs born to consanguineous parents with a multiple congenital anomaly pattern that included low birth weight, tracheoesophageal fistula, duodenal atresia, extrahepatic biliary atresia, hypoplastic pancreas, and hypospadias.
quotes: We studied 2 sibs, born to consanguineous parents, who presented with an MCA pattern which includes low birthweight, tracheoesophageal fistula, duodenal atresia, extrahepatic biliary atresia, hypoplastic pancreas, and hypospadias.

findings.statement: Martínez-Frías et al. (1992) suggested that the constellation of anomalies seen in 2 sibs born to consanguineous parents represented a previously unreported autosomal recessive syndrome.
quotes: This constellation of congenital anomalies appears to be a previously unreported autosomal recessive syndrome.

findings.statement: A computerized search of the Spanish Collaborative Study of Congenital Malformations (ECEMC) by Martínez-Frías et al. (1992) found 3 other unrelated infants with intestinal atresias, hypospadias, and low birth weight. The authors suggested that these infants might represent a milder expression of the same syndrome.
quotes: A computerized search of the data files of the Spanish Collaborative Study of Congenital Malformations (ECEMC) identified 3 other unrelated infants with intestinal atresias, hypospadias, and low birth weight.
These cases may represent a milder expression of the same syndrome.

relevance_reason: The title reports biallelic RFX6 mutations, the gene behind Mitchell-Riley syndrome, causing diabetes with childhood as well as neonatal onset. Only the title was available.

findings.statement: Sansbury et al. (2015) reported that biallelic mutations in RFX6 can cause diabetes mellitus that starts in childhood as well as diabetes that starts in the neonatal period.
quotes: Biallelic RFX6 mutations can cause childhood as well as neonatal onset diabetes mellitus.

relevance_reason: This is the original description of the syndrome: 5 infants with neonatal diabetes, pancreatic hypoplasia, intestinal atresia and gallbladder hypoplasia.

findings.statement: Mitchell et al. (2004) described 5 infants from 3 families (2 sibling pairs and an isolated case) with neonatal diabetes, hypoplastic or annular pancreas, jejunal atresia, duodenal atresia, and gallbladder aplasia or hypoplasia. The parents of one sibling pair were consanguineous. Four children died in the first year of life despite aggressive medical management. One patient with a milder form was surviving without insulin.
quotes: Five infants (two sibling pairs from two families, and an isolated case) presented with neonatal diabetes, hypoplastic or annular pancreas, jejunal atresia, duodenal atresia and gall bladder aplasia or hypoaplasia.
One sibling pair was born to consanguineous parents. One patient with a milder form is surviving free of insulin. Four children died in the first year of life despite aggressive medical management.

phenotypes.text: death in first year of life

findings.statement: Mitchell et al. (2004) performed pancreatic immunohistochemistry on 3 of the infants and found a few scattered chromogranin A-positive cell clusters but complete absence of insulin, glucagon, and somatostatin; exocrine histology was variable.
quotes: Pancreatic immunohistochemistry revealed few scattered chromogranin-A-positive cell clusters but complete absence of insulin, glucagon and somatostatin. Exocrine histology was variable.

phenotypes.text: absence of pancreatic islet hormones (insulin, glucagon, somatostatin)
phenotypes.hpo_label: Abnormality of the pancreatic islet cells

findings.statement: Mitchell et al. (2004) concluded that the combination of anomalies probably represented a new autosomal recessive syndrome. They based this on the affected sibling pairs and parental consanguinity in one family, and suggested a genetic abnormality that interferes with normal islet development.
quotes: This combination of multiple congenital abnormalities has not been previously described and probably represents a new autosomal recessive syndrome involving a genetic abnormality that interferes with normal islet development and whose aetiology is as yet unknown.

findings.statement: In one patient from the consanguineous family, Mitchell et al. (2004) found no duplication or uniparental isodisomy of PLAGL1 at 6q24, no contiguous gene deletion involving the glucokinase gene, and no mutation in the coding sequence or splice sites of PDX1.
quotes: In one case from the consanguineous family, molecular analysis showed no duplication or uniparental isodisomy of PLAGL-1 at 6q24, no contiguous gene deletion involving the glucokinase gene, and no mutation in the coding sequences or splice sites of PDX-1.

relevance_reason: Case report of a consanguineous patient with neonatal diabetes, intestinal atresias and gallbladder agenesis, i.e. the Mitchell-Riley syndrome phenotype. It also proposes autosomal recessive inheritance and reports that candidate genes were negative.

findings.statement: Chappell et al. (2008) reported a patient born to consanguineous parents with neonatal diabetes, intestinal atresias, and gallbladder agenesis, as a further example of a recently described phenotype. They stated that this was the first such case with neonatal diabetes without a demonstrable structural pancreatic abnormality, showing that a deficit in pancreatic function is involved.
quotes: We report a patient born to consanguineous parents as a further example of a recently described phenotype comprising neonatal diabetes, intestinal atresias and gall bladder agenesis.
Our case is the first to have neonatal diabetes without a demonstrable structural pancreatic abnormality, showing that a deficit in pancreatic function is involved.

findings.statement: Chappell et al. (2008) proposed that cases reported elsewhere with overlapping features, including malrotation, biliary atresia, and pancreatic hypoplasia (e.g., as described by Martinez-Frias), may represent variations of the same syndrome.
quotes: Other reports have described cases with overlapping patterns including malrotation, biliary atresia and pancreatic hypoplasia (e.g. as described by Martínez-Frías). We propose that these cases may represent variations of the same syndrome.

findings.statement: Because the patient was born to consanguineous parents, Chappell et al. (2008) concluded that the disorder is likely inherited as an autosomal recessive trait.
quotes: It is likely that this disorder is inherited as an autosomal recessive trait.

findings.statement: In their patient, Chappell et al. (2008) sequenced genes with a known role in monogenic diabetes (KCNJ11, ABCC8, GCK, IPF1, HNF1-beta, NeuroD1, and TCF7L2). They also sequenced a new candidate gene, HNF6, which is involved in hepatobiliary and pancreatic development. They found no mutations in any of these genes.
quotes: We sequenced genes with a recognized role in monogenic forms of diabetes, including KCNJ11, ABCC8, GCK, IPF1, HNF1beta, NeuroD1 and TCF7L2, as well as a novel candidate gene, HNF6, known to be involved in hepatobiliary and pancreatic development, but did not identify mutations.

relevance_reason: Reports a new patient with a novel homozygous RFX6 splice site mutation, gives follow-up on a previously reported patient, and reviews all patients with RFX6 mutations.

findings.statement: Spiegel et al. (2011) reported a new patient with the neonatal diabetes syndrome. The syndrome includes intestinal atresia and hepatobiliary abnormalities. The patient carried a novel homozygous splice site mutation in the RFX6 gene. The authors also gave an update on the clinical outcome of a previously reported patient.
quotes: We report on a new case due to a novel homozygous splice site mutation and update on the clinical outcome of a previously reported patient.

findings.statement: Spiegel et al. (2011) reviewed the clinical and molecular features of all patients with RFX6 mutations; six patients had been reported before their study. They suggested that, despite a fulminant course early after birth, patients who survive may have a relatively favorable prognosis.
quotes: Until now, only six patients harboring RFX6 mutations have been reported.
Our results suggest that despite the early postnatal fulminant course, patients who survive may expect a relatively favorable prognosis.

relevance_reason: The paper reports a new homozygous RFX6 missense mutation (p.V506G) in neonatal diabetes, with functional evidence that it is defective. It also reports work in human beta cells on how RFX6 controls insulin secretion.

findings.statement: Chandra et al. (2014) identified a previously unreported homozygous missense mutation in RFX6 (p.V506G) associated with neonatal diabetes. The mutant protein could not activate the insulin promoter or increase calcium-channel expression.
quotes: We also describe a previously unreported homozygous missense RFX6 mutation (p.V506G) that is associated with neonatal diabetes, which lacks the capacity to activate the insulin promoter and to increase Ca(2+)-channel expression.

findings.statement: Chandra et al. (2014) showed that RFX6 is present in adult human pancreatic endocrine cells. In the human beta-cell line EndoC-betaH2, RFX6 regulated insulin gene transcription, insulin content, and insulin secretion. Knocking down RFX6 lowered expression of calcium-channel genes and reduced L-type calcium-channel activity, which suppressed depolarization-evoked insulin exocytosis.
quotes: We demonstrate the presence of RFX6 in adult human pancreatic endocrine cells. Using the recently developed human β cell line EndoC-βH2, we show that RFX6 regulates insulin gene transcription, insulin content, and secretion.
Knockdown of RFX6 causes downregulation of Ca(2+)-channel genes resulting in the reduction in L-type Ca(2+)-channel activity that leads to suppression of depolarization-evoked insulin exocytosis.

relevance_reason: Mouse conditional knockout study of Rfx6, the gene mutated in Mitchell-Riley syndrome, providing animal-model and pathogenesis evidence about RFX6 function in islet development and adult beta cell function.

findings.statement: Piccand et al. (2014) generated a floxed Rfx6 allele and deleted it in endocrine progenitors with Ngn3-Cre (Rfx6-deltaEndo mice); like the full-body knockout, mutant pups were diabetic and died between 2 and 3 days after birth, with insulin-, glucagon-, somatostatin- and ghrelin-expressing cells nearly absent while PP cells were spared, and with chromogranin A-positive, hormone-negative cells present in the pancreas. The authors concluded that Rfx6 function downstream of Ngn3 is essential for beta cell generation and that impaired beta cell development does not result from defective endoderm.
quotes: Rfx6 is efficiently deleted in Rfx6ΔEndo pancreas (Figure 1G), and like the full-body knockout, Rfx6ΔEndo pups are diabetic and die between 2 and 3 days after birth (not shown).
an endocrine program has been implemented since chromogranin A-positive but hormone-negative cells are found (Figures 1E and 1F)
These findings demonstrate that it is Rfx6 function, downstream of Ngn3, that is essential for β cell generation and that impaired β cell development does not result from defective endoderm.

findings.statement: Piccand et al. (2014) inactivated Rfx6 in adult beta cells of 8- to 10-week-old mice (Rfx6fl/fl;Ins1-CreERT2, Rfx6-deltaBeta) by tamoxifen treatment, achieving 95% deletion within 5 days; the mutant mice did not develop overt diabetes and insulin, c-peptide 1 and c-peptide 2 remained detectable, although Ins1 transcripts were reduced by approximately 54% to 65% while Ins2 was unchanged. The authors concluded that induced inactivation of Rfx6 in a mature beta cell does not preclude insulin production.
quotes: Although Ins1 transcripts were reduced by ∼54%–65% (Table S1; Figure 2H), but not Ins2 (Table S1), insulin peptide, as well as c-peptide 1 and 2, are still detected in β cells lacking Rfx6 as late as 3 weeks after tamoxifen injections (Figures 2A–2F). In agreement with these observations, Rfx6ΔBeta mice do not develop overt diabetes.
Thus, induced inactivation of Rfx6 in a mature β cell does not preclude the production of insulin hormone.

findings.statement: Piccand et al. (2014) found that Rfx6-deltaBeta mice had normal fasting and fed blood glucose but significant glucose intolerance on both intraperitoneal and oral glucose tolerance testing, with markedly reduced first- and second-phase glucose-induced insulin secretion in vivo and reduced glucose- and KCl-stimulated insulin secretion from isolated islets; beta cell mass, alpha cell mass and beta cell proliferation were unaffected.
quotes: In both conditions, mutant mice displayed significant glucose intolerance (Figures 3B and 3C). Impaired glucose homeostasis in Rfx6ΔBeta mice appears not to be due to defects in β cell mass, α cell mass, or β cell proliferation under the same conditions (Figure S3).

However, significant differences were observed following i.p. glucose injection (3 g/kg body weight), as glucose-induced insulin secretion was much less efficient in Rfx6ΔBeta mice (Figure 3D). Both the first- and second-phase responses were reduced in mutant mice.
Clearly, the extent of insulin secretion in response to a glucose or KCl stimulus was reduced in mutant islets compared with controls.

findings.statement: Piccand et al. (2014) showed that islets of Rfx6-deltaBeta mice had strongly reduced Gck (glucokinase) and Abcc8/SUR1 transcripts, together with reduced Ucn3, NeuroD1 and Pax6, while Slc2a2/Glut2, Pcsk1 and Kcnj11/Kir6.2 were unaltered; ChIP-seq and quantitative ChIP in Min6B1 beta cells demonstrated that endogenous Rfx6 binds X-boxes in the Gck promoter and in intron 10 of Abcc8, suggesting that Rfx6 is a direct positive transcriptional regulator of these genes.
quotes: Importantly, we found that transcripts encoding the key genes Gck and Abcc8 were dramatically reduced (Figures 4A and 4B; Table S1).

Quantitative ChIP experiments in nontransfected Min6B1 cells, using an Rfx6 antibody, confirmed that endogenous Rfx6 binds to the Gck and Abcc8 genes, although less strongly to Gck (Figures 4M and 4N). Taken together, our results suggest that Rfx6 is a direct positive transcriptional regulator of Gck and Abcc8
In contrast, the expression of the glucose-facilitated transporter Slc2a2/Glut2, the proconvertase Pcsk1, and the pore-forming unit of KATP channels (Kcnj11/Kir6.2) was not altered (Figures 4C–4E).

findings.statement: Piccand et al. (2014) found by multicellular imaging of intact islets that glucose-induced intracellular calcium responses were reduced by 50% to 60% and glucose-induced cytosolic ATP/ADP increases by about 60% in Rfx6-deleted beta cells; RNA sequencing showed downregulation of eight voltage-dependent calcium channel transcripts (including Cacna1a, Cacnb2, Cacna1d and Cacna1c), and ChIP studies showed Rfx6 binding to X-boxes in intron 1 of Cacna1c and Cacnb2.
quotes: both phases of the intracellular calcium ([Ca2+]i) response to a step increase in glucose concentration were sharply (50%–60%) reduced by Rfx6 deletion (Figures 5A and 5D)

Defects in the latter process were, nonetheless, highlighted by a substantial (∼60%) impairment in glucose-induced cytosolic ATP/ADP increases (Hodson et al., 2014b; Tarasov et al., 2012) (Figures 5F and 5G), consistent with lowered Gck expression.
ChIP sequencing (ChIP-seq) in Min6B1 cells revealed that Rfx6 binds to two of the Rfx6-dependent VDCC genes, at X-boxes in intron 1 of Cacna1c and Cacnb2 genes, respectively (Figures 5K and 5L)

findings.statement: Piccand et al. (2014) reported that 54 of the 68 known "disallowed" genes, normally selectively repressed in mature mouse beta cells, were upregulated in Rfx6-deltaBeta islets, including Slc16a1, Ldha, Pdgfra and Igfbp4, and that Rfx6 bound a conserved region about 10 kb upstream of Ldha; the authors proposed that Rfx6 acts as a master repressor contributing to the maintenance of beta cell maturity and functional identity.
quotes: We found that 54 out of the 68 disallowed genes reported were upregulated in Rfx6ΔBeta islets, including the 11 common genes identified in both studies (Pullen and Rutter, 2013), namely Slc16a1, Ldha, Pdgfra, Igfbp4, Cxcl12, Oat, Smad3, Lmo4, C1qbp, Maf, and Cd302 (Table S3).

ChIP-seq and quantitative ChIP in Min6B1 cells revealed that Rfx6 binds to a conserved region approximately 10 kb upstream of Ldha gene (Figures 6E and 6F), suggesting that Rfx6 could directly regulate the repression of this gene in β cells.
Thus, we propose that Rfx6 is essential to establish and maintain the repression of the disallowed genes and thereby the maturity of β cells.

findings.statement: Piccand et al. (2014) noted that in humans mutations in RFX6 have been reported to cause Mitchell-Riley syndrome, an autosomal recessive syndrome of neonatal diabetes and small bowel atresia, often associated with intestinal malabsorption, and that clusters of chromogranin A-positive, hormone-negative cells have been reported in the pancreas of several patients, suggesting a critical role for RFX6 in the formation of islet and beta cells in humans.
quotes: In humans, mutations in RFX6 have been reported to be the cause of the Mitchell-Riley syndrome, an autosomal-recessive syndrome of neonatal diabetes and small bowel atresia, often associated with intestinal malabsorption (Concepcion et al., 2014; Smith et al., 2010; Spiegel et al., 2011).
Clusters of chromogranin A-positive hormone-negative cells have been reported in the pancreas of several patients, suggesting a critical role for RFX6 in the formation of islet and β cells in humans.

findings.statement: Piccand et al. (2014) suggested, on the basis of their mouse findings, that patients with neonatal diabetes carrying RFX6 mutations are likely to have functional defects in their remaining beta cells in addition to having fewer beta cells, and that it might be worth investigating whether such individuals are susceptible to pharmacologic treatments including sulphonylureas or GLP-1 analogs that could prompt insulin release from the remaining beta cells.
quotes: Finally these results suggest that, in addition to having fewer β cells, sufferers of neonatal diabetes who carry RFX6 mutations are also likely to have defects in those cells that remain (Mitchell et al., 2004).

Whether these individuals may therefore be susceptible to pharmacological treatments, including sulphonylureas or GLP-1 analogs, which could prompt insulin release from the remaining β cells, may be worthy of investigation.
